name: Ahio
overview: Ahio was a male figure in the Old Testament known primarily as the son of Abinadab. He played a role in transporting the Ark of the Covenant by leading the cart on which it was placed. Beyond this, no further tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahio means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the LORD (Yahweh). This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of relationship to God, as noted in 2 Samuel 6:3.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ahio was the son of Abinadab. No other family relationships are detailed beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Ahio is significant in the biblical narrative for his involvement in the transportation of the Ark of the Covenant, an event that underscores the reverence and care given to the sacred object representing God's presence. His role as a leader of the cart carrying the Ark highlights the responsibility entrusted to him and his family. This episode, recorded in 2 Samuel 6:3, situates Ahio within the broader story of Israel's worship and God's covenantal relationship with His people.
